title: Semilinear coactions and linearizations on an affine action groupoid
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H$ an affine group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Write $C=k[H]$, with comultiplication $\Delta$, counit $\epsilon$ and antipode $S$ induced by multiplication, identity and inversion of $H$. Let $E$ be a commutative $k$-algebra with a $k$-algebra map $\rho_E:E\to E\otimes_k C$ satisfying $(\rho_E\otimes1)\rho_E=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_E$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho_E=1_E$. Put $L=E\otimes_k C$, $s^\sharp=\rho_E$ and $t^\sharp(e)=e\otimes1$. The associated affine action groupoid has arrows $(x,h):x\cdot h\to x$, with composition $(x,h)\circ(x\cdot h,g)=(x,hg)$; its identity and composition maps are dual to $\epsilon,\Delta$. For every $E$-module $M$, the formula $\theta(m)=\delta(m\otimes1)$ is a bijection between (i) $L$-linear isomorphisms $\delta:M\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}L\simeq M\otimes_{E,t^\sharp}L=M\otimes_k C$ whose identity pullback is $1_M$ and whose pullbacks along composable arrows satisfy $\delta_a\delta_b=\delta_{a\circ b}$, and (ii) $k$-linear maps $\theta:M\to M\otimes_k C$ such that $\theta(em)=\rho_E(e)\theta(m)$, $(1\otimes\epsilon)\theta=1_M$, and $(\theta\otimes1)\theta=(1\otimes\Delta)\theta$. The inverse bijection is $\delta(m\otimes l)=\theta(m)l$. Its inverse $L$-linear map, in finite-sum Sweedler notation $\theta(m)=\sum m_{(0)}\otimes m_{(1)}$, is
$$m\otimes h\longmapsto\sum m_{(0)}\otimes(1\otimes S(m_{(1)})h).$$
An $E$-linear map of modules commutes with the linearizations if and only if it commutes with their coactions. The correspondence takes the unit module with canonical datum to $(E,\rho_E)$, and the tensor-product datum to the coaction
$$\theta_{M\otimes_E N}(m\otimes n)=\sum(m_{(0)}\otimes n_{(0)})\otimes m_{(1)}n_{(1)}.$$
Tensor products have the meaning in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite type, smoothness, or finiteness assumption on $E$ or $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module), affine translation of its identity and cocycle diagrams. The stated explicit Hopf inverse and tensor formulas are the algebraic expansion of these diagrams and the inverse group law.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] for the coassociative algebra map $\Delta$, counit $\epsilon$, algebra map $S$, and both antipode cancellations. All sums below denote finite presentations of tensor elements, not a basis or a completion. Write $\Delta(c)=\sum c_1\otimes c_2$, $\rho_E(e)=\sum e_0\otimes e_1$, and $\theta(m)=\sum m_0\otimes m_1$. Repeated indices mean application of the specified linear maps to these presentations; equality is equality in a tensor product. Multiplication of coefficients uses [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1), so $(e\otimes c)(f\otimes d)=ef\otimes cd$.

source.place: Tag 022S (definition-group-scheme), affine group-law identities needed for the expansion of Tag 03LF.

proof.text: For $r=s^\sharp$ or $t^\sharp$, let $M_r=M\otimes_{E,r}L$, with its $L$-action as in [def-weil-module-base-change]. For $t^\sharp(e)=e\otimes1$ there is an explicit $L$-linear identification $M_t\simeq M\otimes_k C$: send $m\otimes(e\otimes c)$ to $em\otimes c$, with inverse $m\otimes c\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes c)$. Both respect the tensor relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and their composites fix the displayed generators. On the right $(e\otimes c)(m\otimes d)=em\otimes cd$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property] to $E\xrightarrow{\rho_E}L$, $M$, and this target $M_t$, swapping the two tensor factors to match that lemma's convention. It gives a bijection between $L$-linear maps $d:M_s\to M_t$ (without an invertibility condition yet) and additive maps $\theta:M\to M\otimes_k C$ with $\theta(em)=\rho_E(e)\theta(m)$. Since $\rho_E$ is a $k$-algebra map this is precisely $k$-linearity plus the stated semilinearity. The maps of the bijection are $\theta(m)=d(m\otimes1)$ and $d(m\otimes l)=\theta(m)l$.

source.place: Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module), affine interpretation of the map alpha; algebra.tex Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, for balancing.

proof.text: Pull back along the identity by the algebra map $u_L:L\to E$, $e\otimes c\mapsto e\epsilon(c)$. Since $u_Ls^\sharp=u_Lt^\sharp=1_E$, both pulled-back modules identify with $M$: on a tensor generator the identification is $(m\otimes l)\otimes e\mapsto u_L(l)em$, with inverse $m\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes1$. These formulas respect the tensor relations and compose to the identity by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For the map $d$ of step 2, its identity pullback sends $m$ to $\sum m_0\epsilon(m_1)$. Thus it is $1_M$ if and only if $(1\otimes\epsilon)\theta=1_M$.

source.place: Tag 03LF, identity diagram (2), evaluated on generators.

proof.text:
The coordinate ring of composable arrows $((x,h),(x\cdot h,g))$ is $P=E\otimes_k C\otimes_k C$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes it $L_a\otimes_E L_b$, using $s^\sharp:E\to L_a$ and $t^\sharp:E\to L_b$. The isomorphism is
$$(e\otimes c)\otimes(f\otimes d)\longmapsto\sum ef_0\otimes cf_1\otimes d,$$
with inverse $e\otimes c\otimes d\mapsto(e\otimes c)\otimes(1\otimes d)$. The balancing relation moves $f$ from the second factor to $\rho_E(f)$ in the first; the formulas are inverse on pure tensors, by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the product formula of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Under this identification, pullback along the first arrow, second arrow and composite uses, respectively,
$$p_a(e\otimes c)=e\otimes c\otimes1,\quad p_b(e\otimes c)=\sum e_0\otimes e_1\otimes c,\quad p_{ab}(e\otimes c)=\sum e\otimes c_1\otimes c_2.$$
The first two formulas are the two inclusions into the balanced product; the third is multiplication of the group coordinate, hence $\Delta$.

source.place: Tag 03LF, cocycle diagram (1); schemes.tex Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, for the composable-pair affine ring.

proof.text: Use the maps $p_a,p_b,p_{ab}$ from step 4. The source of the two composite maps is extension of $M$ along $E\to P$, $e\mapsto\sum e_{00}\otimes e_{01}\otimes e_1$; by the assumed coassociativity of $\rho_E$ this also equals $\sum e_0\otimes(e_1)_1\otimes(e_1)_2$. The target is $M\otimes_k C\otimes_k C$. On its source generator $m\otimes1$, the pullback of $d_b$ gives $\sum m_0\otimes1\otimes m_1$ in the intermediate module, and the pullback of $d_a$ then gives $\sum m_{00}\otimes m_{01}\otimes m_1$. The composite-arrow map gives $\sum m_0\otimes(m_1)_1\otimes(m_1)_2$. These formulas follow by substituting the three ring maps into $d(m\otimes l)=\theta(m)l$; all extensions and their identifications send a pure tensor to the indicated product of coefficients by [def-weil-module-base-change] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The source is generated over $P$ by $m\otimes1$, so the cocycle equation is equivalent, in both directions, to $(\theta\otimes1)\theta=(1\otimes\Delta)\theta$.

source.place: Tag 03LF, cocycle diagram (1), both sides computed on a generating tensor.

proof.text:
For a coaction $\theta$ satisfying (ii), step 2 constructs $d$. Before checking its inverse, record the coefficient identity
$$\sum\rho_E(e_0)(1\otimes S(e_1))=e\otimes1.$$
In fact the left side is $\sum e_{00}\otimes e_{01}S(e_1)=\sum e_0\otimes(e_1)_1S((e_1)_2)=\sum e_0\otimes\epsilon(e_1)1=e\otimes1$. These equalities use, in order, the assumed coassociativity of $\rho_E$, the $\mu(1\otimes S)\Delta=u\epsilon$ clause of [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf], and the assumed counit of $\rho_E$. No cancellation of a scalar and no flatness argument is involved.

source.place: Tag 022S, right inverse law, applied after the given algebra coaction; explicit algebraic calculation supporting Tag 03LF.

proof.text:
Define $b:M\otimes_k C\to M_s$ by $b(m\otimes c)=\sum m_0\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}(1\otimes S(m_1)c)$. This is well defined and $k$-linear: it is the composite of $\theta\otimes1$, $1\otimes S\otimes1$, multiplication of the two $C$ factors, and $m\otimes c\mapsto m\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}(1\otimes c)$, all linear maps obtained from the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. It commutes with multiplication by $1\otimes c$ directly. For $e\in E$, semilinearity and multiplicativity of $S$ give
$$b(em\otimes c)=\sum e_0m_0\otimes_s(1\otimes S(e_1)S(m_1)c)=\sum m_0\otimes_s\rho_E(e_0)(1\otimes S(e_1)S(m_1)c)=(e\otimes1)b(m\otimes c).$$
The middle equality is the defining balancing relation in $M_s$, and the last is step 6. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1), pure products of $e\otimes1$ and $1\otimes c$ additively generate $L$, so $b$ is $L$-linear. This proves the required balancing of the inverse, rather than presuming it from the displayed formula.

source.place: Tag 022S, inverse law; Tag 03LF, affine inverse calculation; the formula is an agent-written expansion.

proof.text:
Both inverse composites are explicit. On $m\otimes c\in M_t$,
$$db(m\otimes c)=\sum m_{00}\otimes m_{01}S(m_1)c=\sum m_0\otimes(m_1)_1S((m_1)_2)c=m\otimes c.$$
On the $L$-module generators $m\otimes_s1\in M_s$,
$$bd(m\otimes_s1)=\sum m_{00}\otimes_s(1\otimes S(m_{01})m_1)=\sum m_0\otimes_s(1\otimes S((m_1)_1)(m_1)_2)=m\otimes_s1.$$
In each line coassociativity of $\theta$ gives the second expression; the corresponding antipode identity of [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] and the counit of $\theta$ give the last. Generation by pure tensors is in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $d$ is an isomorphism with exactly the inverse asserted. Steps 3 and 5 supply its identity and cocycle conditions. Conversely those conditions on an isomorphism supply (ii). Step 2 already proves the assignments are inverse bijections, so no choice of tensor presentations enters them.

source.place: Tag 022S, both inverse laws; Tag 03LF, identity and cocycle axioms; explicit inverse compositions.

proof.text: Let $f:M\to N$ be $E$-linear. On the source generator $m\otimes_s1$, the equation $(f\otimes1)d_M=d_N(f\otimes1)$ reads $(f\otimes1)\theta_M(m)=\theta_N(f(m))$. These generators suffice, so the equation for linearizations holds if and only if that for coactions does. The induced maps on both scalar extensions have the formula of [def-weil-module-base-change], and equality on generators follows from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This also checks compatibility with composition and identities of module maps.

source.place: Tag 03LF, morphisms commuting with the equivariance datum, affine generator calculation.

proof.text: For the unit module $M=E$, identify $E\otimes_{E,r}L$ with $L$ by $e\otimes l\mapsto r(e)l$ for either $r=s^\sharp,t^\sharp$. These maps have inverse $l\mapsto1\otimes l$, as their composites agree on pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The canonical unit datum is the identity of $L$ under these identifications. Hence it takes $e\otimes_s1$ to $1\otimes_t\rho_E(e)$, and step 2 associates precisely $\theta_E(e)=\rho_E(e)$.

source.place: Tag 03LF, structure-module datum, computed under scalar extension.

proof.text:
For either $r=s^\sharp,t^\sharp$, the tensor comparison is
$$(M\otimes_E N)\otimes_{E,r}L\simeq(M\otimes_{E,r}L)\otimes_L(N\otimes_{E,r}L),\qquad (m\otimes n)\otimes l\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes(n\otimes l).$$
Its inverse sends $(m\otimes a)\otimes(n\otimes b)$ to $(m\otimes n)\otimes ab$. The $E$-balancing relations on both sides map to multiplication by $r(e)$ and the $L$-balancing relation maps to $ab$; the composites fix the displayed generators. Thus [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] proves these formulas define inverse linear maps. Under them the tensor-product datum is $d_M\otimes_L d_N$, with inverse $b_M\otimes_L b_N$. Evaluation on $(m\otimes n)\otimes1$ gives exactly
$$\theta_{M\otimes_E N}(m\otimes n)=\sum(m_0\otimes n_0)\otimes m_1n_1.$$
The construction of induced bilinear maps under scalar extension is also explicitly stated in [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Tag 03LF, tensoring equivariance maps; algebra.tex Tag 00CX, universal property, for the tensor comparisons.

proof.text:
Check the displayed tensor formula on the quotient and its axioms. Replacing $em\otimes n$ by $m\otimes en$ gives respectively $\sum(e_0m_0\otimes n_0)\otimes e_1m_1n_1$ and $\sum(m_0\otimes e_0n_0)\otimes m_1e_1n_1$; these are equal by $E$-balancing and commutativity of $C$. Multiplying $m\otimes n$ by $e$ therefore multiplies its coaction by $\rho_E(e)$. Counitality follows by multiplying the two counit sums, using multiplicativity of $\epsilon$. For coassociativity, both sides, after using the individual coassociativity equations, are
$$\sum(m_0\otimes n_0)\otimes(m_1)_1(n_1)_1\otimes(m_1)_2(n_1)_2,$$
since $\Delta$ is multiplicative by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Thus the tensor datum has exactly the asserted coaction, including all its axioms. The computations are finite on each element and use neither finite generation nor smoothness; they cover zero modules and the zero algebra $E$ as well.

source.place: Tag 03LF, tensor-product datum; Tag 022S, multiplicativity of the coordinate coproduct and counit; explicit balancing and coassociativity calculations.

lean.statement: theorem hopfCoactionLinearization : ∃ F : Linearization k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ ≃ ModuleCoaction k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ, (∀ (d : Linearization k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ) (m : M), (F d).map m = d.iso (extensionTensor k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ.map 1 m)) ∧ (∀ (θ : ModuleCoaction k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ) (l : E ⊗[k] Γ(H, ⊤)) (m : M), (F.symm θ).iso (extensionTensor k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ.map l m) = targetAction k Γ(H, ⊤) E M l (θ.map m)) ∧ (∀ (θ : ModuleCoaction k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ) (m : M) (h : Γ(H, ⊤)) (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M) (b : Fin n → Γ(H, ⊤)), θ.map m = ∑ i, a i ⊗ₜ[k] b i → (F.symm θ).iso.symm (m ⊗ₜ[k] h) = ∑ i, extensionTensor k Γ(H, ⊤) E M ρ.map (1 ⊗ₜ[k] (HopfAlgebra.antipode k (b i) * h)) (a i))
lean.note: The primary theorem states the bijection and both explicit formulas. The three further theorem declarations state the morphism, unit and tensor clauses of this same node. The two real-data helpers expose Mathlib's canonical coordinate Hopf instance with an unbundled field.
